title: Interaction Surface Harmonization: PRD, Acceptance Matrix, and Launch Orchestration
creator: Evelyn Park
description: Purpose: Harmonize the hosted inference interaction surfaces for generation (chat/completions), embeddings, and reranking so teams can adopt a single, predictable behavioral contract and launch path. This PRD captures the behavioral requirements, acceptance matrix, non-go criteria, scope decisions, and a phased launch orchestration with rollback criteria. Goals: 1) Define consistent request/response contracts (streaming + non-streaming), error semantics, and function/tool-calling expectations across the four surfaces. 2) Ensure performance and quality SLOs are achievable with staged rollout and fallbacks. 3) Provide a prescriptive acceptance matrix and test harness that product/eng/qa can use for sign-off. Out of scope: model training lifecycle, dedicated capacity autoscaling UX, and private on-prem packaging (those are covered in separate initiatives).
background_and_rationale: Customers have reported inconsistent behavior across our existing generation and specialized endpoints: slightly different tokenization heuristics, mismatch in streaming event ordering, and divergent error codes for precondition failures. This creates integration brittleness for SDKs and partner workloads. Harmonizing the surfaces reduces engineering cognitive load and reduces incident surface during rollout of runtime improvements like KV cache and quantization. It also enables a single rollout playbook that the support and SOS teams can rely on.
core_requirements: Uniform API contract: identical top-level fields for request metadata (client_id, request_id, lane, model_hint) and consistent response envelope for final and partial results.
Streaming parity: chunk ordering guarantees (sequence_id, partial=true) and an explicit final chunk marker; SDKs must be able to rehydrate partials into the final response deterministically.
Error taxonomy: canonicalize transient vs permanent errors and surface human-readable 'user_action' when applicable.
Quality guardrails: evaluate generation regressions against baseline prompt set with per-model thresholds, embedding cosine similarity thresholds per workload, and rerank NDCG delta tolerances.
Operational metadata: include token-level timing and cost hints in response headers for telemetry-driven cost attribution in console dashboards.
Backward compatibility: preserve v1 request signatures for 99.5% of calls; provide explicit migration guide for edge cases.
Fallbacks: automatic model-fallback chain for capacity and an opt-out flag for deterministic billing-sensitive customers.
Observability hooks: tracing headers and structured events for query lifecycle, plus eval flagging for sampled requests tied to test prompts.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: A canonical request sample (chat/completion/embedding/rerank) returns the expected envelope in all environments (staging, canary, regional preview) and matches the documented schema.

Quality: Generation quality delta <= 1.5% measured by the PRD prompt set (human-evaluated quality buckets) for each supported model compared to baseline; embedding similarity >= 0.92 cosine on curated datasets; rerank NDCG delta <= 0.02.
Performance: P50 latency within 1.2x of baseline for small prompt lengths and P95 within agreed SLOs for each lane; throughput tests maintain stability under 2x expected traffic burst.
Reliability: Error rate for user-impacting errors remains below 0.1% in canary with synthetic traffic and below 1% during a 48 hour soft-launch with real traffic.
Compatibility: SDK integration tests (Python/JS/go) pass end-to-end including streaming reassembly and function calling behaviors.
Telemetry: Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdown for 24 hours of synthetic traffic; rollout monitoring dashboard configured and linked to escalation runbooks.
Security & Compliance: KMS-backed request audit logs are validated for the private preview customers and SOC review notes addressed.
Docs: Migration guide, API surface contract, and example SDK snippets live in docs.redwood.ai and linked in this ticket.
non_go_criteria: Any model exhibiting >1.5% generation quality regression on the curated human-evaluated prompt set.
Streaming reassembly failures observed in SDKs that cannot be traced to a single deployable fix within the rollout window.
Telemetry gaps preventing reliable cost attribution or missing key identifiers (client_id or request_id) for more than 10% of sampled traffic.
Unresolved security review items flagged by the compliance team for hosted customers with regulatory constraints.
scope_changes_and_tradeoffs: Reduced initial surface: deferred support for multi-modal payload embedding (images + text) to a follow-up project to keep March launch achievable.

Decision to standardize on a single streaming protocol variant (server-sent events with explicit chunk metadata) to simplify SDK implementation at the expense of extra payload framing in the server path.
Opted to limit the first rollout to three model families (small, medium, large) rather than exhaustive model catalog coverage to reduce verification burden.
Tradeoff: stronger quality gates for generation (human-in-the-loop review) will increase rollout time; to mitigate we added a parallel automated evaluation lane to catch obvious regressions earlier.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Integration Validation (staging): internal SDK smoke tests and CI gating against canonical schema (2 business days).

Phase 1 - Canary (region-us-west-2): 1% of traffic with traffic shaping to ensure coverage of chat/completion/embeddings/rerank for diverse prompts (5 days). Monitor errors, P95 latency, and quality hints.
Phase 2 - Gradual Expansion: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over a 10 day window if health metrics stable and quality regression < threshold. Trigger automated rollback on regression breaches.
Phase 3 - Soft Launch: 100% traffic for non-critical lanes, 75% for critical lanes with continued monitoring (48 hours).

Rollback criteria: sustained quality delta > threshold for 2 hours, error spike > 3x baseline for 15 minutes, or any SDK-breaking streaming reassembly bug reported by more than 3 customers in 12 hours.
Communication: pre-scheduled customer advisory, blog post for breaking changes, and dedicated PST hours for SEs during canary to handle integration questions.
test_plan: Unit and integration tests for canonical envelopes and error taxonomy (automated).
E2E SDK tests for streaming reassembly across Python/JS/Go with fuzzed chunk ordering.
Performance regression suite: token-level throughput tests with KV cache variations and quantized kernels enabled.
Quality evaluation: human-reviewed sample of 1,200 prompts across verticals with A/B comparison against baseline; automated metrics for embedding similarity and rerank NDCG.
Chaos tests: simulate slow downstream model responses and partial Xfer interruptions to validate graceful degradation and fallback chains.
Security tests: audit log tamper checks, KMS integration smoke, and permission boundary verification for private-preview tenants.
